name: Microsoft Defender: isolate device
description: Run from a case: find the case's device in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint by name and isolate it from the network (full isolation; the device keeps talking to Defender only), then record the result in a case note and on the playbook task. A case without a device name gets a note instead.

params.label: Entra tenant ID
params.help: Directory (tenant) ID from Entra admin center > Overview.

params.label: Defender API host
params.help: api.security.microsoft.com, or the regional host closest to your tenant: eu.api.security.microsoft.com, us.api.security.microsoft.com, uk.api.security.microsoft.com, au.api.security.microsoft.com. Host only, no https://.

secrets.name: DEFENDER_CLIENT_ID
secrets.description: Application (client) ID of the Entra app with WindowsDefenderATP Machine.Isolate.

secrets.name: DEFENDER_CLIENT_SECRET
secrets.description: Client secret value of that app registration.

setup:
## Entra side
1. Entra admin center > App registrations > **New registration** (single tenant, no redirect URI).
2. API permissions > Add a permission > **APIs my organization uses** > search **WindowsDefenderATP** > **Application permissions**: `Machine.Read.All` and `Machine.Isolate`.
3. **Grant admin consent for <tenant>** (application permissions do nothing until an admin consents).
4. Certificates & secrets > **New client secret**; copy the secret *value*. Note its expiry date.

One app registration can serve both Defender response workflows (isolate and release) when it has both permissions. It is separate from the Graph app used by *Microsoft 365 Defender: pull alerts* only if you want to keep read and response rights apart.

## Here
1. Settings > Secrets: add `DEFENDER_CLIENT_ID` and `DEFENDER_CLIENT_SECRET`, each allowed for **both** `login.microsoftonline.com` (token request) and your Defender API host (the OAuth token is bound to the same hosts as the secrets that obtained it).
2. Install with `AZURE_TENANT_ID` and `DEFENDER_API_HOST`.

Token: `POST https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/oauth2/v2.0/token`, `grant_type=client_credentials`, `scope=https://api.securitycenter.microsoft.com/.default`. Microsoft requires this legacy audience even on `api.security.microsoft.com`; any other scope answers 403.

## Which device
The case's `hostname` attribute (create the custom artifact type `hostname` in Settings > Artifact types and add the device to the case). Without it, the device in the newest Defender alert promoted into the case (`deviceEvidence.deviceDnsName` of a *Microsoft 365 Defender: pull alerts* alert). The name is lowercased and must match Defender's `computerDnsName` **exactly** (often the FQDN, e.g. `ws-01.contoso.com`); a short name that Defender stores as an FQDN finds 0 devices and nothing is sent. Names containing a quote or backslash are refused.

## How it works
- `find`: `GET /api/machines?$filter=computerDnsName eq '<name>'&$top=2`.
- `isolate`: only when exactly one device matches, `POST /api/machines/<id>/isolate` with `{"Comment": "SOC Hub case #<id>: <title>", "IsolationType": "Full"}`. Defender answers **201** with a machine action. For selective isolation (Outlook, Teams and Skype keep working; Windows 10 1709+), change `IsolationType` to `Selective` in the step.
- A case note records both HTTP statuses and the machine action id. The action finishes when the device checks in; follow it on the device page in security.microsoft.com (Action center).

## Limits
Microsoft allows 100 calls per minute and 1,500 per hour for these APIs. A device Defender hasn't seen within the retention period isn't found.

## Playbook tasks
Run from a case task (a playbook task linked to this workflow), the last step records the outcome on the task and ticks it when Defender accepted the action (HTTP 201); a skipped or refused attempt is recorded and the task stays open.

Docs relied on: [Isolate machine](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/api/isolate-machine), [Release device from isolation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/api/unisolate-machine), [List machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/api/get-machines), [App without a user](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/api/exposed-apis-create-app-webapp), [deviceEvidence](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/security-deviceevidence?view=graph-rest-1.0).

## Containment guardrails
A **containment guard** step runs first: devices protected in **Settings → Integrations → Containment guardrails** (VIPs, domain controllers, critical ranges) are never isolated automatically, and the tenant's daily and per-case caps apply. A refusal stops the run and adds a case note; the isolation is listed on the case under **Artifacts & assets → Containment**, where an analyst marks it released once undone.
